options.queryReplacement: ={{ [ JSON.stringify($json.briefs.map(b => ({ change_id: b.change_id, status: b.status, applicability: b.applicability, priority: b.priority, brief: b.brief, verification: b.verification }))) ] }}

parameters.content:
## Regulatory change tracker · AI & data governance
Checks regulator **sources** in any market (EU, US, UK, AU, ZW, …), detects **new and amended** publications (collector service, no AI), screens them with **Claude Haiku**, and writes a **brief** for each relevant one with **Claude Opus**: dates, obligations and affected **controls**, each backed by a quote.

**Code checks every quote word for word**, every date and every control before a person reviews it. Approved changes become **Jira tasks** per control owner.

- `POST /webhook/reg/run` · `GET /webhook/reg/review` · `POST /webhook/reg/decide` · `GET /webhook/reg/report`
- Credentials: Postgres (reg_tracker), Anthropic, Jira

### Cost control
Unchanged sources cost nothing. One cheap Haiku call screens every change; Opus only briefs relevant ones, capped by `maxBriefs`. A source's first check is a **baseline**: no changes, no AI.

### The model proposes, the code decides
"Verify briefs" removes any quote not found word for word in the document, any date its quote doesn't state, any control not in the library, and flags the brief for the reviewer. Applicability and priority come from the company profile, in code.
Jira tasks (upper branch) run before the response (lower branch), so the response lists the new task keys.
